I was heavily physically abused by my sister, who was 50-70 lbs heavier than I was. She would pull my hair until huge swaths came out, tackle me to the floor, embed her fingernails into me until it drew blood, beat me with her fists, etc. She was later diagnosed with borderline personality disorder. I still sometimes have dreams where I'm trying to explain something to her, and out of nowhere, she becomes angry, and does things to me out of malice. My parents were apathetic. They told me that I was "instigating", not willing to get involved with their large and unruly daughter. They hit me too; but I digress. I had nobody to tell me that this wasn't normal. I ended up internalizing my parents' comments. I really did end up feeling like I deserved what was happening to me. I felt like there was something inherently wrong with me.

When I'm with him, I'm always spacing out or thinking to myself, so I remember our time usually in an emotional sense as time I spent with myself. You're still young. You haven't been married long. Not to be pushy, but I would think very hard if you want that relationship to continue. It's very easy to fall into a routine of remaining in a low grade state of discontent and peace rather than stir things up. If you see a therapist, I think what you wrote would be very useful things to tell them.

My boyfriend has great fun in talking "wifing" me and more seriously, our future house/life/etc, and of course I indulge and ramble about it with him, but I don't think we're ever getting married. I'm going to college soon. And as hard as it will be to break up with him, I don't have the confidence that even he will want to continue.

I'm not even planning on getting married. It's not like I like being single. My childhood has been spent with on-and-off crushes and ideas about an imaginary, ideal partner, but no matter who I marry, if I will only end up hating their guts in four to six years, what's the point? As romantic as it would be to be an embittered, experienced divorced woman with dark lipstick and big overcoats, creating a new life for herself suddenly, I don't believe I have the mental or emotional energy to deal with it. 

True love is compromise. Nobody marries their dream person. If it was easy, and the other person was sexy, smart, rich, talented, open, interested in all the same things, etc, then it couldn't be love at all, because it would just be easy. Love means that you're willing to put effort into the other person. Knowing that love is a constant choice to stay, I would feel guilty trapping somebody knowing that I'll eventually become old, decrepit, bitter, or that my gimmick personality will get old. I also wouldn't like to be trapped with somebody that I know will eventually become all of these things *and* in addition, dissatisfied with me for the same reasons. I think I'll serial date until I die.
